transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I'm having a really hard time at work lately. I do bookkeeping, and... well, I just can't stop going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again. 

It's gotten so bad that I'm staying at the office for hours after everyone else leaves. Even when I know I've already checked the numbers, I just get this overwhelming feeling that if I don't do it one more time, something bad will happen and it'll be completely my fault. It's just getting to be too much.
Do these urges to recheck come with thoughts that feel intrusive and unwanted?

Yeah, they definitely do. It's like... even after I know the numbers match, this thought just keeps jumping in that I missed one hidden mistake somewhere in the payroll or taxes. I start thinking that somebody's check won't go through, or the firm will get in huge trouble. I try really hard to push the thought away, but it just comes right back. It's like I can't even trust my own eyes anymore.
Do you feel that all this rechecking is excessive, even though you still feel compelled to do it?

Yeah, I do. I know it's way too much. Like I was saying before, staying at work for hours after everyone else leaves just to look at the exact same spreadsheets... I know it doesn't make sense. 

I know I already checked the calculations. But I just can't stop going back over them again and again. Even when I tell myself it's excessive and I need to go home, I still have to do it. Because if I don't check it just one more time, I get that awful feeling that something bad is going to happen and it'll be entirely my fault.
On a typical workday, about how much time do you spend rechecking the spreadsheets?

I'm not really sure of the exact amount, to be honest. I haven't timed it or anything. I just know it's... it's a lot of hours. 

Once I start going back over everything, I kind of lose track of the clock. So I couldn't give you a specific number, just that it keeps me there way past when I'm supposed to clock out, and it basically takes up my whole evening.
Have these checking behaviors started to significantly interfere with your work or daily life?

Yeah, it really has. It's... it's causing some major problems. I actually missed a filing deadline recently because I couldn't stop checking, and I got called into a formal meeting with my boss about it. And outside of work, it's pretty much ruined my schedule. I've stopped going to my choir rehearsals, and I can't make it to my volunteer commitments at the youth center anymore. I just... I can never get out of the office on time to actually go to them.
If you resist rechecking the spreadsheets, do you feel a strong urge that you must do it to prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah, exactly. If I try to just close the laptop and walk away, the feeling is just... it's overwhelming. I get this intense thought that there's a mistake I missed, and if I don't go back and check it that one more time, the whole company's finances are going to be messed up, and it will be completely my fault. The urge is so strong that I can't ignore it. I just have to go back and look at the calculations again to try and make that feeling go away.
Do these repeated checks feel like something you want to do because it’s the right way to be careful, or do they feel unwanted and against your wishes?

They definitely feel unwanted. I don't want to be doing it at all. Even after I've checked and I know the numbers match, this... this thought just keeps jumping into my head that I missed one hidden mistake somewhere in the payroll or the taxes. I'll start worrying that somebody's check won't go through or the firm will get in trouble. I try to push the thought away, I really do, but it just comes right back. It's honestly like I can't even trust my own eyes anymore.
Do you get the same kind of unwanted urge to check things over and over in other parts of your life besides work?

No, not really. It's... it's pretty much just at work. I haven't really noticed that same urge to check things over and over when I'm at home or doing other stuff. It really just seems to be tied to the numbers and the accounts at the office.
Did this problem start soon after something stressful changed at work?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I'm not really sure, but nothing major really changed at the office. I didn't get a new position or a different boss or anything like that. Work is just the usual amount of busy. It just kind of... started happening on its own, I guess. I can't really point to one specific stressful thing that set it off.
Before this started, have you generally seen yourself as a perfectionistic person who needs things done exactly right?

No, I wouldn't say so. I mean, I try to do a good job, but I've never really been a perfectionist. Before all this started, I would just do my work, make sure it looked okay, and move on. I never really had this feeling that every little thing had to be exactly perfect. I was just kind of... normal about it, I guess.
